does anyone relate to this?

i don’t know what’s going on with me. i just want someone to listen to me and offer any thoughts at all. i’ve never opened up about this so it would really help. one thing i struggle with a lot , is this weird fixation on contamination . i’ll give an example. it often shows up around this one thing i really care about and enjoy a lot. at one point, it made me genuinely happy and felt like a safe, positive thing in my life. maybe because of that, i’ve always felt a lot of pressure around it … like I need to protect it from any negativity or bad memories. its been a bit intense at times. and after some moments where i felt embarrassed or like i made mistakes in spaces connected to it, my brain has started to link those feelings to the thing itself. now when i try to just love it, i get intrusive thoughts, feelings that it’s somehow “tainted” or ruined, or like i’m not allowed to enjoy it anymore? i dont know. more so, i struggle a lot (a lot lot lot) with intense anxiety around like … past mistakes or embarrassing moments, and how they reflect on me as a person. this is a daily struggle for me. memories come at me all of the time, no matter what i do or where i am, and i feel stuck trying to figure out if they were truly wrong, how bad they were, or whether they could come back to affect me in the future. a big part of this is an overwhelming fear of being exposed, or “cancelled,” … even though i’m not a public figure? it might not make sense, but it’s constant. i review every single thing i do, trying to assess how it makes me look, whether or not it could come back to bite me. i’m terrified to have a social media presence, or just doing anything worthwhile in the real world because of the possibility that it could come crashing down. i always feel like i need to hide !!!! like i am so, so guilty, all of the time, and i don’t even truly know why. i understand that it may be irrational but i CANNOT stop the feeling and worries. i feel i have to be extremely careful with what I say and share, even to my closest friends. i’m always going back and deleting messages that i think could be misinterpreted or misconstrued, or deleting people who i feel are “unsafe”. i’m afraid to have arguments because they might one day use it to shame me infront of the whole world. i’ve even lost friends because i felt they knew too much about me and would use it against me. .\_\_. i just worry that if i’m not careful enough, i could make things worse or create new problems. i also worry that it’s too late. like: an example of this, is i’ll think about friendships or interactions i’ve had with people who were younger than me, thinking about the years between us, anything i said or did that could possibly be read as creepy, or fearing that they will find me in the future and expose me as a creep for things that i said or did. i’m just terrified that i’ve been inappropriate and i feel like i can’t do anything because i will get exposed for it someday and my whole entire life will be ruined. i think about this literally all the time. there’s more than just the examples i wrote, i think … these are just the things i felt like getting off my chest. basically, my mind is a prison i can’t escape LOL. man, i would do anything to stop this feeling. if you read this and have any advice at all, thank you

What brings you in today? I’m really interested in hearing what’s on your mind.

You know what the worst part is? It's not just about being anxious in general; it's this specific, weird fixation on something I actually love. Like, there was one thing—maybe a hobby or an activity—that used to make me genuinely happy. I felt safe with it. But then, after some moments where I felt embarrassed or made mistakes connected to it, my brain completely rewired itself. Now, whenever I try to enjoy it again, intrusive thoughts pop up saying it's "tainted" or ruined. It feels like I'm not allowed to enjoy it anymore because of those past errors.

And honestly, it goes way beyond just that one thing. The anxiety

That sounds incredibly heavy—feeling like your joy is now blocked by thoughts that weren’t there before. It’s so powerful how something that used to bring you safety can suddenly feel like it’s tainted, even when you’re trying to return to it.  

What would it mean, for you, to just *feel* safe again in that space—without needing to prove anything or avoid mistakes? I’m curious—what’s one small thing you might notice if you allowed yourself to go back to that activity, even just a little, without judgment?

That's a really hard question to answer honestly, because the thing I'm most afraid of is that if I just *do* it without being perfect, the feeling of being "exposed" will crash down on me instantly.

If I allowed myself to go back to that activity—even just for five minutes—without judging my past mistakes or worrying about what someone else might think later... I would probably feel this intense wave of panic rising in my chest. My heart would race so fast I'd have to stop breathing, and then immediately after, I'd start scanning my mind for any tiny detail from before that could be used against me. Like, "Wait, did I say something weird last time? Did they laugh at me? What if they remember now?"

It sounds like your body is holding onto a deep sense of fear—like you’re still waiting to be seen or accepted, even after the moment has passed. That panic, that racing heart, isn’t just about the past—it’s about the belief that if you show up, even imperfectly, you’ll be judged or rejected again.  

And it’s really brave of you to admit that you’d need to sit with that feeling, just to begin. What would it feel like, in that moment, if you didn’t have to explain or defend yourself at all—just to be present, without needing to fix or prove anything?

Honestly? I don't know if I can even imagine it without my brain immediately trying to sabotage the feeling.

If I could just sit there, do that thing, and *not* have a million voices in my head saying "What if they remember?" or "Did I look weird?", I think I'd feel... empty? Or maybe just terrified of being alone with myself for once. Usually, when I try to engage in something like this, I'm hyper-aware of every single movement, every word, every micro-expression. I'm constantly checking if I'm doing it "right" so I don't get caught.

So if I stopped needing to explain or defend myself... I guess I'd feel a huge weight lift off my shoulders, but then immediately replace it with this gnawing guilt. Like, "Why am I feeling relief? Am I forgetting how bad things were? What if I let myself feel happy again and then regret it

That’s such a powerful and honest reflection—the relief you’re describing isn’t just a feeling of freedom, it’s a kind of disconnection from the story you’ve been telling yourself for so long. And the guilt you feel afterward? That’s not a sign of weakness—it’s your mind trying to protect you from the unfamiliar, quiet space of just being with yourself without needing to justify anything.  

So, if you could sit with that moment—where you’re not checking, not explaining, not scanning—what would it feel like to simply *be* there, without needing to fix or explain it? Just be with the stillness?

It's terrifying to even think about that stillness, honestly. My brain is so used to running on high alert, like a siren in the background, that silence feels dangerous. It feels like if I just stop checking and start *being*, someone might come out of the shadows and expose me right then and there.

If I could just sit there without needing to fix anything... I think my chest would feel really tight at first. Not from fear, but from this crushing sense of "what have I done?" or "how am I allowed to exist right now?" It would feel like holding my breath underwater. Every instinct I have is screaming to pull away, to hide, to delete everything, to run.

Because admitting that means acknowledging that the whole time, I've been terrified of *existing* in front of others without armor.

It would make me feel less like a monster who needs to be contained, and more like someone who's just come home

Knowing that the cracks are maps... instead of failures.

It would make sense of why I'm here, why my brain is so loud, why I have this specific, paralyzing fear about being "exposed" for things I did years ago. In that quiet sunlight on the cracks

And if you could just stand in that light, without needing to fix the past or run from it—what would it feel like to know that every shadow you’ve carried was just the ground beneath your feet, not a sign that you were lost?

Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sl.evidence:
Saying it out loud... that feels like stepping into the open field after walking through a forest of thorns for years.

If I say, *"I'm not running to avoid falling, I'm running to avoid being seen,"* I think my voice would shake at first. It wouldn't be a confident statement; it would sound fragile, like glass about to crack. Because admitting that means acknowledging that the whole time, I've been terrified of *existing* in front of others without armor.

But if I could actually say it and just let it hang there... instead of immediately worrying about how people will react or if they'll use it against me, I think the immediate urge to apologize would stop. The internal monologue that usually goes, *"No, no, you're wrong, they won't judge you"* would be replaced by something quieter. Something that just says, *"Okay. I see why I'm doing this."*
